REGULAR MEETING AGENDA
CITY COUNCIL OF THE CITY OF CERRITOS
AND THE SUCCESSOR AGENCY TO THE CERRITOS REDEVELOPMENT AGENCY
THURSDAY - AUGUST 23, 2018 - CITY HALL -
07:00 P.M.
City Council Chamber
AGENDA MATERIALS: Reports and materials related to items on this Agenda are available for public inspection at the City Clerk's Office, Cerritos City Hall, 18125 Bloomfield Avenue, Cerritos, CA 90703, during normal business hours, 8 a.m. to 5 p.m., Monday through Friday, Telephone (562) 916-1248. Materials submitted to the City Council/Successor Agency after distribution of the agenda packet are available for public inspection in the City Clerk's Office at the above address during normal business hours as noted.
PUBLIC COMMENTS: For all Agenda Items, except for Consent Calendar Items, public comments will be allowed at the time each matter comes up for discussion. Please complete and submit a blue Speaker's Card to ensure that you are recognized when the Agenda item is considered. The general public comments portion of the meeting, under Agenda Item 6, will not exceed 45 minutes, and no speaker will be allowed more than five minutes, unless determined appropriate by the Chair. To assist in the preparation of appropriate responses, persons are requested, but not required, to state their name and city of residence for the record.
PUBLIC HEARINGS: Public hearings will be conducted in the order indicated on the agenda, unless otherwise directed. Please complete and submit a blue Speakers Card if you wish to present testimony. Conduct of public hearings will occur in substantially the following sequence: the item to be heard is announced, a report of written correspondence and staff report are received, and the City Council asks questions of staff. The public hearing is opened and verbal testimony will occur in the following order: the applicant, if applicable, those in favor, opposed, or interested parties, and rebuttal by applicant. Speakers are requested, but not required, to state their name and city of residence for the record. After verbal testimony, the public hearing is closed and the matter is deliberated with a determination being made or a continuation of the matter.

MINUTES OF A REGULAR MEETING OF THE CERRITOS CITY COUNCIL AND THE
SUCCESSOR AGENCY TO THE CERRITOS REDEVELOPMENT AGENCY HELD ON
AUGUST 23, 2018, IN THE COUNCIL CHAMBERS AT CERRITOS CITY HALL, 18125
BLOOMFIELD AVENUE, CERRITOS, CALIFORNIA

1.  Call to Order

  The meeting was called to order at 7:00 p.m.

2.  Invocation

  The invocation was given by Pastor Michael Voytek, Rehoboth Reformed Church.

3.  Pledge of Allegiance

  The Pledge of Allegiance was led by Matthew Borroto and Madison Eugenio –
  Recreation Services Division Youth Sports League Scorekeepers.

4.  Roll Call

  The following members of the City Council/Successor Agency were in
  attendance:

  Council/Agency Member Jim Edwards
  Council/Agency Member Grace Hu
  Council/Agency Member Frank A. Yokoyama
  Mayor Pro Tem/Vice Chair Naresh Solanki
  Mayor/Chair Mark E. Pulido

5.  Presentations/Appointments

5A.  A Proclamation was given to:

  Blanca Verdin (Life-saving actions related to her service as a “Cerritos on
  Wheels” driver).

  Presentations to Blanca Verdin from:

  Christopher Craig (Field Representative - 58th Assembly District)
  Lynda Johnson (Field Deputy to Los Angeles County Supervisor Janice Hahn).

6.  Public Comments and Suggestions

  David Pylman spoke regarding business discussed at City Council meetings and
  ABC Unified School District elections.

  Case Van der Linden expressed concern with the extension of the Metro through
  Cerritos.

7.  Consent Calendar
  Items under the Consent Calendar are considered routine and will be enacted by
  one motion. There will be no separate discussion of these items unless a
  Council/Agency Member or citizen so requests, in which event the item will be
  removed from the Consent Calendar and considered separately.

7.  Consent Calendar (continued)

7A.  Approval of Minutes

  Approval of the City Council/Successor Agency Regular Meeting Minutes of
  August 9, 2018 (COUNCIL/SUCCESSOR AGENCY).

  MOTION: It was moved by Edwards, and seconded by Solanki, to approve the
  City Council/Successor Agency Regular Meeting Minutes of August 9, 2018
  (COUNCIL/SUCCESSOR AGENCY).

  The motion carried (5 – 0) as follows:

  AYES:  Edwards, Hu, Yokoyama, Solanki, Pulido
  NOES:  None
  ABSENT:  None
  ABSTAIN:  None

7B.  Approval of the Register of Demands

7B.1  Approval of the Register of Demands for the City of Cerritos dated August 23,
  2018 (COUNCIL).

  MOTION: It was moved by Edwards, and seconded by Solanki, to approve the
  Register of Demands as follows (COUNCIL):

  City of Cerritos  8/23/2018  $2,367,319.88

  The motion carried (5 – 0) as follows:

  AYES:  Edwards, Hu, Yokoyama, Solanki, Pulido
  NOES:  None
  ABSENT:  None
  ABSTAIN:  None

7B.2  Approval of the Register of Demands for the Successor Agency to the Cerritos
  Redevelopment Agency dated August 23, 2018 (SUCCESSOR AGENCY).

  MOTION: It was moved by Edwards, and seconded by Solanki, to approve the
  Register of Demands as follows (SUCCESSOR AGENCY):

  Successor Agency  8/23/2018  $  3,991.00

  The motion carried (5 – 0) as follows:

  AYES:  Edwards, Hu, Yokoyama, Solanki, Pulido
  NOES:  None
  ABSENT:  None
  ABSTAIN:  None
 City of Cerritos  August 23, 2018
City Council/Successor Agency  Page 3 of 7

7.  Consent Calendar (continued)

7C.  Approval of the Treasurer’s Reports

  Approval of the City Council/Successor Agency Treasurer’s reports for the
  period ending July 31, 2018 (COUNCIL/SUCCESSOR AGENCY).

  MOTION: It was moved by Edwards, and seconded by Solanki, to approve the
  City Council Treasurer’s reports for the period ending July 31, 2018
  (COUNCIL/SUCCESSOR AGENCY).
  The motion carried (5 – 0) as follows:

  AYES:  Edwards, Hu, Yokoyama, Solanki, Pulido
  NOES:  None
  ABSENT:  None
  ABSTAIN:  None

8.  Public Hearings

8A.  Recommendation by the Cerritos Planning Commission, on a vote of 4-0-1, with one
  Commissioner abstaining, to approve the following:

  Review and consideration to waive full reading of and adopt A RESOLUTION OF
  THE CITY OF CERRITOS APPROVING CONDITIONAL USE PERMIT 2018-2, A
  REQUEST BY VIMARN THAI MASSAGE TO PERMIT A MASSAGE ESTABLISHMENT
  USE WITH STATE-CERTIFIED MASAGE THERAPISTS AT 20110 PIONEER
  BOULEVARD, SUITE D, CERRITOS, CALIFORNIA, 90703.  THE SUBJECT
  PROPERTY IS ZONED NEIGHBORHOOD COMMERCIAL (CN) (APN 7055-017-023)
  (COUNCIL).*

  *Pursuant to Section 15301 of the California Environmental Quality Act (CEQA),
  this project is categorically exempt from CEQA review.

  Councilmember Yokoyama recused himself from participating in this agenda item
  stating his property is within 500 feet of the subject property. He then left the dais
  and the Council Chamber for the remainder of the item.

  A staff report was given by Robert A. Lopez, Current Planning Manager.  A
  PowerPoint presentation was displayed.

  Matthew and Pimba Pa Anderson, applicants/owners of Vimarn Thai Massage,
  spoke regarding services to be provided at the business.

  The Mayor opened the public hearing and public comments.

  David Pylman complimented staff regarding City project updates. He also noted
  massage parlor employment procedures and City codes.

  Noting there were no further individuals who elected to speak, the Mayor closed the
  public hearing and public comments.

  (continued next page)
 City of Cerritos  August 23, 2018
City Council/Successor Agency  Page 4 of 7

8.  Public Hearings (continued)

8A.  (continued)

  MOTION: It was moved by Hu, and seconded by Solanki, to adopt Resolution
  No. 2018-15, A RESOLUTION OF THE CITY OF CERRITOS APPROVING
  CONDITIONAL USE PERMIT 2018-2, A REQUEST BY VIMARN THAI
  MASSAGE TO PERMIT A MASSAGE ESTABLISHMENT USE WITH STATE-
  CERTIFIED MASSAGE THERAPISTS AT 20110 PIONEER BOULEVARD,
  SUITE D, CERRITOS, CALIFORNIA, 90703. THE SUBJECT PROPERTY IS
  ZONED NEIGHBORHOOD COMMERCIAL (CN) (APN 7055-017-023)
  (COUNCIL).

  The motion carried (4 – 0) as follows:

  AYES:  Edwards, Hu, Solanki, Pulido
  NOES:  None
  ABSENT:  Yokoyama (recused)
  ABSTAIN:  None

  At the conclusion of this item, Councilmember Yokoyama returned to the
  Chamber and resumed his seat on the dais.

9.  New and Old Business
9A.  Review and consideration to designate a Voting Delegate and Alternate(s) for the
  League of California Cities Annual Conference to be held September 14, 2018, in
  Long Beach, California (COUNCIL).

  A staff report was given by Vida Barone, City Clerk.

  The Mayor opened public comments. Noting there were no individuals who
  elected to speak, the Mayor closed public comments.

  MOTION: It was moved by Hu, and seconded by Yokoyama, to designate
  Councilmember Yokoyama as the voting delegate and Councilmember Hu as the
  alternate for the League of California Business Meeting to be held September 14,
  2018 (COUNCIL).
  The motion carried (5 – 0) as follows:

  AYES:  Edwards, Hu, Yokoyama, Solanki, Pulido
  NOES:  None
  ABSENT:  None
  ABSTAIN:  None

9B.  Review and consideration of a request for authorization to increase the City of
  Cerritos’ community funding contribution to the Cerritos Regional Chamber of
  Commerce (COUNCIL).

  A staff report was given by Kristin Aguila, Advance Planning Manager.

  The Mayor opened public comments.

  (continued next page)
 City of Cerritos  August 23, 2018
City Council/Successor Agency  Page 5 of 7

9.  New and Old Business (continued)

9B.  (continued)

  Scott Smith, Chamber Executive Director, thanked the City for support of the
  Cerritos Regional Chamber of Commerce and explained the role and operations
  of the Chamber.

  Paul W. Bellenbaum inquired as to the name of the Mayor at the time of the City
  name change from Dairy Valley to Cerritos.

  Noting there were no further individuals who elected to speak, the Mayor closed
  public comments.

  ORIGINAL MOTION: It was moved by Hu, and seconded by Edwards, to
  authorize the immediate allocation of $7,500, thereby reinstating the City’s total
  annual community contribution to the Cerritos Regional Chamber of Commerce
  of $75,000 annually.

  SUBSTITUTE MOTION (ADOPTED): It was moved by Yokoyama, and
  seconded by Edwards, to increase the immediate allocation to $13,500,
  increasing the City’s total community contribution to the Cerritos Regional
  Chamber of Commerce to $81,000 for the 2018-2019 Fiscal Year (COUNCIL).
  The substitute motion carried (4 – 1) as follows:
  AYES:  Edwards, Yokoyama, Solanki, Pulido
  NOES:  Hu
  ABSENT:  None
  ABSTAIN:  None

9C.  Review and consideration of a request for authorization for a purchase of two
  utility vehicles and two riding mowers (COUNCIL).

  A staff report was given by Todd Kuh, Parks Superintendent.

  The Mayor opened public comments. Noting there were no individuals who
  elected to speak, the Mayor closed public comments.

  MOTION: It was moved by Edwards, and seconded by Solanki, to:

  1.  Authorize the expenditure in an amount not to exceed $52,542 for the
  purchase of two utility vehicles from Stotz Equipment; and

  2.  Authorize the expenditure in an amount not to exceed $67,209 for the
  purchase of two mowers from Turf Star; and

  3.  Allocate new funding in the 2018-19 Fiscal Year budget toward the utility
  vehicle and mower purchases (COUNCIL).

  The motion carried (5 – 0) as follows:

  AYES:  Edwards, Hu, Yokoyama, Solanki, Pulido
  NOES:  None
  ABSENT:  None
  ABSTAIN:  None
 City of Cerritos  August 23, 2018
City Council/Successor Agency  Page 6 of 7

9.  New and Old Business (continued)

9D.  Review and consideration of the repair and maintenance of the holiday
  decorations to be funded through the Art in Public Places Trust Fund (COUNCIL).

  A staff report was given by Kanna Vancheswaran, Director of Public Works.

  The Mayor opened public comments. Noting there were no individuals who
  elected to speak, the Mayor closed public comments.

  MOTION: It was moved by Solanki, and seconded by Edwards, to:

  1.  Authorize the appropriation and expenditure of $50,000 from the Art in
  Public Places Trust Fund for the repair and maintenance of the holiday
  decorations; and

  2.  Authorize the City Manager to execute a contract with Pac Rim
  Resources for the refurbishment work; and

  3.  Authorize the City Manager to execute any change orders necessary to
  complete the project (COUNCIL).

  The motion carried (5 – 0) as follows:

  AYES:  Edwards, Hu, Yokoyama, Solanki, Pulido
  NOES:  None
  ABSENT:  None
  ABSTAIN:  None

10.  Legislative Items

  None.

11.  City Council Communications/Committee Reports/Report on Meetings

  Reports were provided by Councilmembers Edwards, Hu, and Yokoyama, Mayor
  Pro Tem Solanki, and Mayor Pulido.

  CONSENSUS (Hu): Direct staff to place an item on the next regular meeting
  agenda to consider moving the Regular City Council/Successor Agency meeting
  of Thursday, October 11, 2018 to a Special City Council/Successor Agency
  meeting on Monday, October 8, 2018.

  CONSENSUS (Solanki): Direct staff to cancel the Special Meeting of the City
  Council/Successor Agency scheduled for Monday, September 10, 2018 due to
  lack of items.

  CONSENSUS (Pulido): Directed the City Manager to research the City policy
  related to offering financial rewards for information related to violent crimes.
 City of Cerritos  August 23, 2018
City Council/Successor Agency  Page 7 of 7

12.  Closed Session

  The City Council did not recess to Closed Session to discuss any items.

12C.  PUBLIC EMPLOYEE PERFORMANCE EVALUATION
  Pursuant to California Government Code Section 54957 (COUNCIL)
  Title: City Clerk

13.  Adjournment

  The meeting was adjourned in memory of Fine Arts and Historical Commissioner,
  Smita Das. The meeting was adjourned at 8:55 p.m.
